subject: literature
passage: By the time the afternoon wind came up over the rooftops of the old ______ Bilal and his younger brother Saad had already untangled their kite strings three times. Saad wanted to fly the red kite, the one with the long paper tail, and Bilal wanted to fly it too, which was how the tangles had started. In the end they flew it together, Bilal holding the spool and Saad calling out the gusts, and the kite climbed until it was a red fleck above the minarets and the water tanks.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: "By the time the afternoon wind came up over the rooftops of the old city" is a long introductory phrase, not a complete sentence; the main clause is "Bilal and his younger brother Saad had already untangled their kite strings." An introductory phrase of this length is followed by a comma.
explanation.A: Correct. A comma separates the long introductory phrase from the main clause that follows.
explanation.B: Incorrect. A semicolon must have an independent clause on both sides, but the introductory phrase is not one.
explanation.C: Incorrect. A colon must follow a complete independent clause; the introductory phrase is incomplete.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The introductory phrase has no main clause of its own, so the period leaves a fragment.
